terms.definition: Controlled Unclassified Information. Government information that isn't classified but still has to be protected, such as technical drawings or contract details your customer marks as CUI.
Multifactor authentication. Signing in with a password plus a second proof of identity, such as a code from a phone app or a security key.
Virtual private network. A secure, encrypted connection from a device outside the office into the company network.
Federal Information Processing Standards. U.S. government standards; FIPS 140 covers encryption. FIPS-validated means a product's encryption was tested and approved under that standard.
System security plan. The document that describes the systems that handle CUI and how you meet each requirement.
Mobile device management. Software that sets and enforces security settings on company laptops, phones, and tablets.
Data loss prevention. Tools that recognize sensitive information and block or warn when someone tries to send it somewhere it shouldn't go.
Demilitarized zone. A separate network for systems the public can reach, such as a web server, walled off from your internal network.
Voice over Internet Protocol. Phone calls made over the internet, such as with a cloud phone service.
Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement. The Department of Defense's rules for its contracts, including the cybersecurity clauses that point to NIST SP 800-171.
